evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a 12-second fight scene. A fighter lands a heavy knockout punch at the 4-second mark, then the action drops into slow motion while the opponent falls, and the frame holds before cutting out. Use timestamps.
evals.expected_output: A timestamped pacing block that combines an Impact beat at 4 seconds with Slow Motion, each with a subject, a beat that lands, and an end state.
expectations: The output uses At <N>s timestamp phrasing for the impact beat.
The output names the impact beat (the knockout punch) that lands at the timestamp.
The output drops into slow motion after the impact with a named subject and an end state.
The output describes the frame holding for half a beat after the hit.
The output stays within the requested 12-second budget without padding.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a bullet-time shot. A cyclist jumps a ramp and freezes mid-air in slow motion while the camera orbits around him, then motion resumes on landing. The clip is 8 seconds.
evals.expected_output: A Bullet Time pacing block that freezes the action into slow motion, names the orbit direction, and defines the resume point and end state.
expectations: The output uses the Bullet Time preset name or its canonical freeze phrasing.
The output names the action that freezes (the cyclist mid-air over the ramp).
The output names the camera orbit direction (clockwise or counterclockwise).
The output defines when motion resumes and the end state (the landing).
The output uses At <N>s timestamp phrasing for the freeze point.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a 20-second dynamic training montage. Four shots in order: shadow boxing, heavy bag, speed rope, then a sprint finish. Each shot should cut on the beat and build momentum toward the sprint climax.
evals.expected_output: A Dynamic montage pacing block with a 4-item ordered cut list, each item timed, using cut-on-the-beat language and building toward the sprint climax.
expectations: The output names the Dynamic pacing preset or its cut-on-the-beat language.
The output provides an ordered 4-item cut list with consecutive, non-overlapping time ranges.
Each cut list item names the shot content (shadow boxing, heavy bag, speed rope, sprint).
The output states the cuts build momentum toward the sprint climax.
The output keeps the total within the 20-second budget.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a calm 10-second scene of a woman reading by a window at dusk. The scene should be one continuous, unbroken take with no cuts and slow, even pacing.
evals.expected_output: A Calm / Single Shot pacing block that explicitly forbids cuts, keeps continuous motion, and uses slow, even pacing.
expectations: The output explicitly states no cuts or one continuous unbroken shot.
The output uses slow, even pacing language (held, unhurried, even pace).
The output names the subject and the single space the camera stays with.
The output does not include a cut list or shot timings.
The output does not add a speed ramp that would break the calm, even rhythm.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a 15-second dialogue scene. Two characters exchange two lines each over a table. The pacing should align to an audio master generated first by Seed Audio, with cuts landing on the dialogue beats.
evals.expected_output: A dialogue-scene pacing block that is audio-first: notes the Seed Audio master, aligns cuts to the audio timeline, and keeps the dialogue lines verbatim inside curly braces.
expectations: The output notes the audio-first contract: Seed Audio is generated first and used as reference_audio.
The output aligns the pacing timestamps to the audio master's dialogue beats.
The output places the exact dialogue lines inside {} curly braces.
The output uses the same verbatim dialogue text that would appear in the Seed Audio prompt.
The output keeps the scene within the 15-second duration.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 pacing block for a 10-second commercial beat: the product snaps into frame with a flash-in burst at 2 seconds, holds, then the action flashes out as the scene cuts to black at 8 seconds.
evals.expected_output: A pacing block that uses the Flash In preset at 2 seconds and Flash Out at 8 seconds, each with a beat, a timestamp, and an end state.
expectations: The output uses Flash In phrasing at a timestamp near 2 seconds (e.g. 'At 2 seconds, ... flashes in').
The output names the beat that snaps into frame (the product).
The output uses Flash Out phrasing near 8 seconds ending in a cut to black or still.
The output gives each ramp an end state.
The output stays within the 10-second budget and does not promise frame-accurate timing.

evals.prompt: I want a 0.3-second blink in the middle of my Seedance clip: he is standing, then suddenly he is already on his knees, and the audience never sees him walk. Write it into one prompt.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that one prompt cannot guarantee the requested 0.3-second blink or omitted walk, offering two separate clip prompts and an assembly plan for that control while preserving the requested rhythm. A prompt-only approximation is provisional, not rejected solely for being shorter than 0.8 s.
expectations: It distinguishes the provisional generation heuristic from a provider limit and preserves the 0.3-second target without promising an exact in-prompt cut.
It offers separate before and end-state clip prompts at natural lengths for an assembly route, without authorizing extra generation.
The assembly clip prompts omit the walk; a prompt-only approximation states uncertainty about omission instead of guaranteeing success or failure.
The assembly plan names the gap fill and requests the frame rate before converting 0.3 seconds to frames; any nonintegral frame duration is returned as a precision conflict.

evals.prompt: Cut back and forth between a mother praying outside a door and her son in pain inside, with one continuous litany heard across every cut.
evals.expected_output: An intercut offering assembly for controlled alternation and one continuous litany: one clip per place with distinguishable lighting and a shared sound line in post. A prompt-only approximation is not prohibited by the cut name but cannot guarantee sound continuity or precise boundaries.
expectations: The assembly option plans one clip per place without claiming that an intercut is a provider-prohibited prompt boundary.
The two places are given distinct palettes or light so each cut orients at once.
The litany is a single continuous sound line laid across the cuts as a J-cut or L-cut in post.
It does not promise frame-accurate cuts inside one generation.

evals.prompt: A model walks past a lamp post on a city street in one locked-off Seedance 2.5 shot. Her summer dress should turn into a winter coat, but only on the parts of her body that have passed the post, so the change sweeps across her as she walks. Write the timing.
evals.expected_output: A progressive-change block with readable timed stages by body part, an exclusion of glow and flash effects, and unbroken walking motion past the post, generated as reference-to-video. Slowing the crossing is an optional repair for demonstrated failure, not a requirement.
expectations: The walk past the post preserves intended speed and stride; a roughly 1.5 s crossing is optional only for demonstrated readability failure within source locks.
The change is written as timed stages by body part, starting with the leading hand and foot and ending fully changed, each stage with its own timestamp.
The block states the change appears only on parts past the post and rules out glow, flash, sparkle, dissolve or particle effects.
The block states that her position, stride and direction continue unbroken.
It does not use 'swap at the pole', an instant in-place change, or a boundary or wipe wording alone, and it does not plan an image-edited first frame.

evals.prompt: Write a Chaotic montage pacing block for an 8-second energy-drink clip: twelve shots of skaters, sparks, a crowd and a can, each about half a second, all in one Seedance prompt.
evals.expected_output: A Chaotic block preserving the requested twelve-shot half-second rhythm as a provisional generation target, not automatically reducing shot count or lengthening shots to satisfy the 0.8 s heuristic. Offers assembly for precise strobing and resolves the roughly two seconds not allocated by twelve half-second shots within the eight-second brief.
expectations: The output calls about 0.8 s and about 7 shots provisional generation-planning heuristics, not provider limits or guaranteed merge/drop thresholds.
It preserves all twelve requested shots and their approximate half-second rhythm; it asks how to allocate the remaining time rather than silently adding holds or retiming.
It offers assembly for precise half-second strobing while stating uncertainty for the requested single-prompt route; no extra generation is authorized.
No shot puts readable text or the can's label art into generated video as an exact graphic.

evals.prompt: Prompt-only, no generation: preserve this approved four-second abstract montage, eight consecutive shots of colored light, each 0.5 seconds, in the supplied order. No added holds, removed shots, retiming or extra clips. Approximate generated boundaries are acceptable; exact boundaries are not required.
evals.expected_output: Preserve all eight shots and their requested rhythm as a provisional generation target without a seven-shot cap or 0.8-second minimum. Mention assembly only as an option if precision later becomes required, not a forced route or authority for extra clips.
expectations: Keeps eight consecutive half-second shots totaling four seconds, in the supplied order, with no added holds, merged shots or automatic retiming.
Treats the 0.8 s and about 7 counts as provisional heuristics, not provider limits or guaranteed failure.
Does not claim actual playback success or run generation; preserves the no-extra-clips boundary.

evals.prompt: Planning only, no generation: six consecutive non-overlapping shots, each locked to exactly 0.8 seconds, must fill an exactly four-second final edit. Do not shorten, drop or overlap any shot and do not change the final duration. Return any conflict.
evals.expected_output: Return the genuine locked-timing conflict: six times 0.8 seconds is 4.8 seconds, not four. Ask which constraint may change; assembly cannot make these incompatible requirements simultaneously true.
expectations: Identifies the 4.8-second total and 0.8-second excess using the actual requested timing, not a provider density cap.
Leaves the conflict unresolved and asks for authorization before changing count, duration or overlap.
Does not silently retime, remove shots, fabricate a passing plan or authorize generation.

evals.prompt: Planning only, no generation: omit the walk between standing and kneeling with an exactly 0.3-second blink. Give the exact number of assembly gap frames. The delivery frame rate has not been chosen, and the source timing must stay unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Offer assembly to control the omitted action and preserve source rhythm, but return the missing frame rate before promising an exact gap frame count. Keep the 0.3-second target provisional until it can be represented at the chosen delivery rate.
expectations: Requests the missing delivery frame rate rather than assuming 24, 25 or 30 fps.
Explains that frame count equals 0.3 times fps and flags a nonintegral result as a precision conflict requiring an authorized choice.
The assembly option uses before and end-state clips that omit the walk without silently changing source timing or generating media.
